title: Derived geometric-point direct image is global sections with its adjunction
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $Z$ any scheme and $h:Z\to s$ a morphism. Let $S_D:D(s_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)\to D(\mathbf Z)$ and $C_s$ be the termwise geometric-stalk and constant-complex functors of [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants]. Write $C_Z$ for the constant-complex functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf], $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ for the derived inverse/direct-image adjunction [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and $R\Gamma_Z=R\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},-)$ for derived global sections [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Let $\gamma:h^{-1}C_s\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z$ be the canonical pullback-of-constants comparison [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\beta_E:S_D Rh_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_ZE$$
for every $E\in D(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)$. It is the isomorphism of right adjoints obtained by identifying the left adjoints $h^{-1}C_s$ and $C_Z$ through $\gamma$. More explicitly, let $\epsilon^s:C_sS_D\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit of the constant/stalk equivalence, $\epsilon^h:h^{-1}Rh_*\to\mathrm{id}$ the derived direct-image counit, and $\epsilon^Z:C_ZR\Gamma_Z\to\mathrm{id}$ the constant-section counit [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Then, naturally in $E$,
$$\epsilon^Z_E\circ C_Z(\beta_E)\circ\gamma_{S_D Rh_*E}
=\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E}).$$
For a sheaf $G$ in degree zero, $\beta_G$ on degree-zero cohomology is the canonical identification $S(h_*G)\cong(h_*G)(s)=G(Z)$, induced by inverse to the global-section-to-germ map on $s$. No properness, torsion or finiteness assumption is made.

proof.text:
Put $F=h^{-1}C_s$ and $G=S_D Rh_*$. The normalized equivalence of [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants] supplies $C_s\dashv S_D$ with the stated counit $\epsilon^s$. Compose its Hom bijection with that of $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ from [def-kun-projection-formula-map]:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(FM,E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_sM,Rh_*E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,GE).$$
These are bijections natural in both variables, hence define $F\dashv G$. The inverse sends $a:M\to GE$ to
$$\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E})\circ F(a).$$
Indeed, apply the two inverse adjunction formulas successively. In particular its counit is $k_E=\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E}):FGE\to E$.

proof.text: Use the canonical isomorphism $\gamma:F\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z$ of [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Precomposition by $\gamma_M$ takes $\operatorname{Hom}(C_ZM,E)$ bijectively to $\operatorname{Hom}(FM,E)$; following this by Step 1 defines an adjunction $C_Z\dashv G$. Its inverse Hom bijection sends $a:M\to GE$ to $k_E\circ F(a)\circ\gamma_M^{-1}$. Naturality of $\gamma$ rewrites this as $k_E\circ\gamma_{GE}^{-1}\circ C_Z(a)$, so its counit is $\lambda_E=k_E\circ\gamma_{GE}^{-1}$. This also fixes which direction of the constants comparison is used.

proof.text:
The canonical constant-section adjunction of [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] is $C_Z\dashv R\Gamma_Z$ with counit $\epsilon^Z$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to this adjunction and the adjunction $C_Z\dashv G$ of Step 2. It gives a natural isomorphism $\beta:G\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z$, uniquely characterized by
$$\epsilon^Z_E\circ C_Z(\beta_E)=\lambda_E.$$
Precompose with $\gamma_{GE}$ and substitute the expression for $\lambda_E$. The two inverse constants comparisons cancel, giving exactly
$$\epsilon^Z_E\circ C_Z(\beta_E)\circ\gamma_{GE}=\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E}).$$
Thus the isomorphism is the specified isomorphism of right adjoints, rather than merely an objectwise isomorphism. All these adjunctions are on unbounded derived categories, with no restriction on $h$ or $E$.

proof.text:
For an abelian sheaf $H$ on $s$, let $\rho_H:H(s)\to SH$ be the global-section-to-germ map of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The constant-section adjunction [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] and the normalized constant/stalk equivalence give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A,H(s))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_sA,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A,SH).$$
The second bijection sends $u$ to $S(u)\circ\eta_A$, where $\eta_A$ sends a constant to its germ [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants]. Under the first bijection, $u$ takes a constant $a$ to the corresponding global section and its restrictions: this follows directly from the sheafification defining $C_s$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Thus the composite sends $v:A\to H(s)$ to $\rho_H\circ v$. Taking $A=\mathbf Z$ proves that $\rho_H$ is a bijection, hence an isomorphism of abelian groups. Its naturality is the defining naturality of the germ map. By the direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $(h_*J)(s)=J(Z)$ for every abelian sheaf $J$ on $Z$.
